observed.name: ProbeTcp6Format
observed.first_line: VERDICT: confirm — the byte-order defect is real on this host (kernel 7.2.11, x86_64 little-endian). /proc/net/tcp6 prints each 32-bit word of the address in host byte order, so the frozen `_listen_inodes` never recognises `::1` or `::ffff:127.0.0.0/104` and `port_owned_by` returns `None` for both. IPv4 127/8 returns `True` as it should.

observed.name: ScoutRfc4291Mapped
observed.first_line: VERDICT: confirm — RFC 4291 §2.5.5.2 is 80 zero bits ‖ 16 one bits (`FFFF`) ‖ IPv4; §2.5.3 is `0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1` (`::1`); `::ffff:127.0.0.0/104` is exactly 127.0.0.0/8 mapped; and this host proves `/proc/net/tcp6` prints each 32-bit word byte-reversed, so the frozen `_listen_inodes` matches neither encoding.
